source.title: Neural substrates of appetitive and aversive prediction error

confidence_rationale: Review of causal and recording evidence that prediction error both up/down-regulates associations and allocates attention to stimuli, across dopamine, amygdala, vlPAG, hippocampus, cortex and LC-NA, for both appetitive and aversive outcomes. Supports the two-role framing (RW and attention) and the distributed aversive PE system; not specific to per-cue associability.
failure_signatures: Aversive PE is distributed across several systems (vlPAG, amygdala, LC-NA, dopamine); an architecture that routes all aversive credit through one module misrepresents the biology.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Prediction error up- and down-regulates associative relationships and allocates attention to stimuli; its neural substrates for both appetitive and aversive outcomes span mesolimbic dopamine, amygdala, vlPAG, hippocampus, cortex and locus coeruleus noradrenaline.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports the claim's premise that aversive PE does two jobs (update and attention allocation). The LC-NA component is close to MECH-074a's arousal gain, i.e. MECH-598's broadcast control, so the review also reminds us that biology has both the broadcast and the selective route.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Broad review; does not adjudicate Pearce-Hall vs Mackintosh or per-cue associability specifically. Named in the intake; low mapping fidelity for the specific mechanism.
mapping.source_context: Review of rodent and human causal and recording studies

confidence_components.notes: Useful orientation; low specificity to MECH-598's distinctive content.
